defects: B-BARE (render-1, seed 1): branch ramification lacks defining beech structure — primary and secondary limbs run as long, near-unbranched straight wands with only thin filamentous twigs at the tips, instead of the dense, repeatedly forking fine twig network that fans into broom-like sprays throughout the crown in the leaf-off reference (reference-1, left panel). This is the largest believability gap and reads as a different taxon at silhouette level.

B-WHOLE (render-0, seed 1): crown is thin and see-through — sky and bare limb runs are visible across most of the canopy and foliage resolves as scattered small dots — whereas the beech whole-tree references (reference-0) show dense, opaque foliage carried in stacked horizontal layers with a solid shaded interior. This follows the same sparse skeleton in the shared geometry group, so the foliated view fails on the same defining structure.

B-WHOLE and B-BARE (render-0, render-1, shared geometry group c1781092...:seed:1): the bole carries repeating horizontal ring/band seams along its full height, most visible on the lower trunk. The beech bark reference (reference-1, right panel) is continuously smooth grey with irregular lichen flecking and no transverse banding; the regular periodic repeat is a construction/texture artifact rather than bark character, and it sits below the uniform-surface finish floor of the catalogue anchor (anchor-0).
observations: Broad, rounded, slightly wider-than-tall open-grown crown outline is acceptable natural variation for Fagus sylvatica — reference-0 shows both a narrower forest-grown habit (left) and a broader park-grown habit (right), so crown outline itself is not a gap.

Smooth, unfissured trunk surface with a single dominant bole persisting into the lower crown is a correct beech reading and matches reference-1 (right panel) at the structural level; only the periodic banding on that surface is objectionable.

Trunk tone in both renders is a chalky near-white with a cool cast, lighter than the silvery grey of reference-1; this may be the render's lighting/exposure rather than an albedo choice, so it is recorded as an uncertain optional refinement and does not block.
Lichen/scar flecking on the bole, leaf blade shape and marginal serration are optional detail refinements at this viewing distance; their absence alone would not block.
Backdrop, ground plane and shadow treatment are stylistically consistent with the catalogue anchor (anchor-0); no lighting or presentation regression was observed.

The two views are mutually consistent: the limb skeleton visible through the thin canopy in render-0 corresponds to the skeleton in render-1, as expected for one identity and seed with foliage hidden rather than an unloaded leaf-off build.
No claim is made that reference-0 and reference-1 show the same specimen or a seasonal change in one tree; they are treated as independent documentation of species character.
Photorealism was not applied as a criterion and no pixel-level or identical-shape match to the photographs was required or expected.

findings.observation: Required cell reference_character / B-WHOLE / seed 1: the foliated crown is sparse and transparent, with sky visible between scattered small leaf clusters and bare limb runs exposed across the canopy, where the beech whole-tree references show dense opaque foliage in stacked horizontal tiers with a dark shaded interior.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Optional and not required for the finding: too few terminal twigs in the shared skeleton to carry a closed canopy.

findings.observation: Required cell reference_character / B-BARE / seed 1: crown ramification consists of long, straight, seldom-dividing limbs carrying only wispy tip filaments, while the leaf-off reference shows branches subdividing repeatedly into a dense fine twig system that fills the crown volume. The defining beech twig architecture is absent, not merely less detailed.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Optional: insufficient terminal branching order / sub-branch recursion during generation.

findings.observation: Both views show regular horizontal ring seams repeating along the smooth bole; the bark reference shows an unbroken smooth grey surface with irregular lichen flecks and no periodic transverse structure.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Optional: trunk mesh ring/segment boundaries or a tiling UV repeat in the bark material.

findings.observation: A single dominant smooth bole rising into the crown before dividing into heavy ascending limbs is present in both renders and matches the open-grown beech habit documented in the references.
Overall crown envelope (broad, rounded, with low limbs retained on one side) falls within the habit range shown across the two reference panels for this species.

Cross-view constraint holds: the limb layout seen through the thin canopy in the foliated view corresponds to the leaf-off skeleton, consistent with one geometry group at seed 1 with foliage visibility toggled.
Trunk albedo reads chalky near-white rather than the silvery grey of the bark reference; the direction of the mismatch is visible but its cause is not resolvable from the packet.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Optional: lighting/exposure rather than material colour.

findings.observation: Fine bark detail (lichen flecks, healed scars) and leaf blade/margin detail visible in the references are not resolved in the renders at this scale.

Presentation finish (background, ground plane, shadow, anti-aliasing) is comparable to the accepted catalogue anchor, applied to finish/style only and not to species morphology; no style-level regression observed.
